paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : The performance on BioGPT.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) on BioGPT varies as a function of the co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick labels at 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3 (with the axis starting near 0 and extending beyond 10^3), and the lines are drawn at four co-occurrence values visually located around 5, 30, 300, and 3000. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from 25% to 60%, with labeled ticks at 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, and 55. The Base series is a black solid line with circle markers that rises from about 28.5% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 30.8% at the second point and about 32.2% at the third point, then remains about 32.2% at the largest co-occurrence value. FT is a blue solid line with downward triangle markers increasing from about 32.0% to 35.7% to 37.2% to 38.4% across the four x positions. IKE is a red solid line with upward triangle markers increasing from about 32.6% to 37.6% to 39.5% to 41.3%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers increasing from about 36.5% to 40.8% to 44.8% to 45.3%. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon-like markers increasing from about 36.0% to 43.0% to 45.8% to 46.6%. ROME is a green solid line with square markers increasing from about 43.7% to 49.2% to 56.0% to 58.8% across the x-axis range.
